sense.text:
The times of temptation are not only the trials coming from outside, from Trump, Netanyahu and the politics of the last days. Now that things are being set in motion that will try our faith, we have to look out for each other, and before we can do that we have to look out for ourselves: the trials and tribulations within ourselves.

“He that hath small understanding, and feareth God, is better than one that hath much wisdom, and transgresseth the law of the most High.” Small understanding is the brother who does not know a lot of the scriptures, who is not really a precept guy, but he fears God. Much wisdom is the one who knows the scriptures, understands the Bible and the commandments, and breaks the laws of God anyway. The first is better.

It is good to know about Trump, the last days, the prophecies and the current events of the world. But the most important thing to truly know is how to apply and keep God’s laws, and to know what is going on in here, in the heart and the mind.

precepts.why:
“Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away.” This is how the man of much wisdom comes to transgress the law. The wine here goes two ways. It is literally liquor: you go to the club, they serve the liquor, everyone gets drunk and loose, and things take place that should not. And it is doctrines. So the man of small understanding who fears God is better than the man of much wisdom who falls for women and wine, women and doctrines, which make men of understanding to fall away.

“And he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent.” Impudent is not a common word among us. It means not showing due respect for another person: impertinent, insolent, cheeky, audacious, brazen, shameless, presumptuous, disrespectful, insubordinate, irreverent, flippant, rude, ill-mannered, ill-bred, fresh, cocky, brass-necked, lippy, mouthy, sassy. The man who deals with harlots, who dabbles in a bunch of women, becomes disrespectful.

You see it in the Israelite community: men who dabble in whoredom, whether the alleged polygamy they push, which is cosplay, an act, or men dealing with actual prostitutes. They attack and insult this congregation because it teaches monogamy, one wife, calling us homosexuals, while they are dealing with a bunch of women. And what you hear in their speech and teaching matches the words of impudent: ill-bred, fresh, disrespectful. They know how to debate and argue back and forth, but their understanding is very minimal.

They are beyond irrelevant; they are only the example. The point is within ourselves: when you dabble in wine, whether liquor or doctrines, or in women and prostitution, you become impudent and you begin to fall away from the understanding of the scriptures.

sense.text:
“Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence.” Concupiscence is strong sexual desire, lust: lustfulness, sexual appetite, sexual longing, sexual passion, libido, sex drive, the biological urge, lechery, excessive or offensive sexual desire. It goes right back to wine and women making men of understanding fall away, and to the men that dabble at harlots: they tend to be concupiscent.

It goes to the porn. A lot of brothers deal with that spirit of porn, and brothers and sisters young and old have fallen victim to it so excessively that the spirit of concupiscence comes upon them and they start to lose their minds. It affects their behavior, their mental state and their marriage. Some brothers in here are battling porn so much they begin to despise their spouse, because they are looking at the woman on the screen and saying my wife looks nothing like that, and they push away their loved ones.

When you watch porn, porn watches you too. The eyes are the windows of the soul, and when you open your eyes to these things, they open themselves to you. The demons and spirits on those people in the video jump on you. And it evolves: it starts as one thing and it grows like a drug, like the weed that is not strong enough anymore so you upgrade. The dopamine is a drug. Porn, food, alcohol, sex, money: they are copes for low self-esteem, anger and personal issues a man refuses to bring forward.

Married or single, porn is found among us. That concupiscent spirit has been with many of us a long time; many were exposed to sex very early, and being exposed to such mature content so young puts a stronger sexual urge upon you down the line. This is not an attack. It is us reasoning in the scriptures. The prayer is for God to turn concupiscence away, “and thou shalt hold him up that is desirous always to serve thee.”

“Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me.” They go hand in hand. The greediness of the belly is food and drink; the lust of the flesh is the sexual desire. Lust and greed are synonymous: it is all a habit, and you keep feeding it and it gets bigger and bigger. When it takes hold of you, you are so consumed in it you cannot stop yourself: so consumed in food and liquor you are morbidly obese and cannot walk half a mile, so consumed in porn that you cannot stay up. A virgin who has never had a woman and does that excessively conditions his body to itself, at its own speed and pace, not to a spouse; the mind knows the difference between a woman and a hand, and it ends in letting off immediately, in erectile dysfunction.

Don’t let it take hold of you to the point where you say, I can’t fight it, I keep falling, I’m not coming to the school anymore, I’m no good. That is what Satan wants you to believe. You better hop your ass in the shower, rinse yourself off, and come to the school. Let it take hold and you begin to despise yourself and your loved ones, and it evolves until you are in cuffs, from the heterosexual to the rape one, the incest one, the child one, because they will find you. Or it leads you to want the actual thing, out in the streets looking for harlots.

“And give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind.” See what it leads to: the impudent mind, the same as with wine and women and harlots. You grow disrespectful. You are cursing your wife out, telling her you don’t want her anymore, put me on child support, ready to destroy your whole house for what you watch. When you are told, brother, you’re fat, sister, you’re big, you get mad, and Satan tells you you are just big boned. Nobody ever found a fat skeleton. Big boned is a lie with reason.

That is why he says give not thy servant into an impudent mind: you begin to reject those who tell you that you are battling lust, of the belly or of the flesh. Satan already has you convinced: I’m good, I got it under control. Usually who you are is the answer to all your problems. You know yourself better than anybody: you know if you are big, if you are lustful, if you are battling porn. When you deny the problem is there, that is when the problem starts.

precepts.why:
This is the spiritual side of it: the mind is a door, and the eyes are the windows to the soul. “Behold, I stand at the door, and knock.” Christ is not talking about the door of your house. The door is your spirit, your mind. That is the righteous side.

But there is a left-hand side too. When you watch porn, Satan is at the door, knocking: open up to the incest, the homosexual, the lesbian, the threesome, the violent porn, the rape porn, the child porn. Each time you watch, you crack the door a little more. Satan waits; you open it more and more until he can fit, and then he calls in the rest: come on in, hatred, violence, pedophile. Now you have personalities, you are talking to yourself, hearing and seeing things, because you opened that door piece by piece. Sin has taken hold of you.

“If any man hear my voice, and open the door”: who opens the door? You do. You let the spirit of God in, or you let something else in. It is your decision. “I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.” It goes the same with Satan: open the door to him and he will enter you and sup with you, and convince you that you should not go to the school, that you should sit in self-pity, remorse and hatred.

He plays in your head: they don’t understand me, they’re married, they’ve got wives, they don’t go through what I go through. Some men battle that thing while married, but Satan convinces you it is only you, no one understands, so stay to yourself, you don’t need help. When you hear that in your head, that is Satan. Any excuse in your mind is not God. Excuses are lies with reason. That is how lust takes hold of a man.

sense.text: “For they shall eat, and not have enough: they shall commit whoredom, and shall not increase: because they have left off to take heed to the Lord.” This is Ephraim, the northern kingdom. Ephraim went into idolatry, and with idolatry comes sexual behavior, lust. Eating and not having enough is the greediness of the belly; committing whoredom is the lust of the flesh.

“Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the heart.” Whoredom and wine is the same thing as wine and women in Sirach 19:2; that is where the writer got it from. Whoredom is women and prostitution, and new wine is liquor itself, and they take away the understanding. Pornography is whoredom. Prostitutes are whoredom. Sleeping around with a bunch of women and calling them wives is whoredom.

Examine the men they use to substantiate polygamy. If one wife is gay, then Adam, the first man, was gay. Noah had one wife, and Shem, Ham and Japheth had one wife each, and the Lord delivered all of them. Abraham had one wife, Sarai, and only took Hagar because Sarah, old and unable to have children, told him to take her handmaid as a surrogate to bring forth an heir. Isaac had one wife. Jacob wanted Rachel and was tricked into taking Leah, and only came to four because the wives gave him their handmaids when their wombs were closed.

And look at their wealth. Abraham had 318 servants born in his house, land from the Nile to the Euphrates, iron, brass, gold, livestock: hundreds upon hundreds of sheep and oxen. He did not ask Sarah to go half on the light bill. Abraham took care of his wife and her slave on his property; Isaac took care of Deborah and Rebekah from his father’s wealth; Jacob took care of four women on his land. David and Solomon were kings who ruled and reigned, whom nobody could tell what to do about marriage. Show me a captive in the scriptures who had wives. Nowhere.

All of our forefathers who had multiple wives kept them on their estate, under their roof, and maintained them financially. If you have a wife in Jersey, one in Philly, one in Cali and one in Chicago, all paying their own bills, that is not your wife; that is some girl you call wifey. Captive Negroes cannot accomplish that. It is make-believe polygamy, and it is whoredom, and over time whoredom and wine take away the heart: you become arrogant and lose understanding.

precepts.why:
This is the contest of the three young men, the bodyguards of the Persian king: the first spoke of wine, the second of the king, and the third, Zorobabel, spoke of women and of the truth. Zorobabel says, “Is he not great that maketh these things? therefore great is the truth, and stronger than all things.” The truth is stronger than all things. “All the earth calleth upon the truth, and the heaven blesseth it: all works shake and tremble at it, and with it is no unrighteous thing.”

“Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked.” Wine is wicked especially if it is drunk to excess. That is why they call liquor spirits: the more you indulge, the more you are taken out of your spirit into a different one, a happy one, a violent one, a depressed one, a crazy one. So you must drink in moderation, or wine becomes wicked. The king in excess is wicked, women in excess are wicked, and all men are wicked: “and there is no truth in them.” The prophets always put these in the same category: wine, women, the king, and men.

“As for the truth, it endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore.” With her “there is no accepting of persons or rewards; but she doeth the things that are just, and refraineth from all unjust and wicked things.” The home of the truth is the Bible and nothing else, and it is refrained from all unjust and wicked things. “She is the strength, kingdom, power, and majesty, of all ages”: the truth leads to the kingdom, to power, and to majesty, rulership in all ages. God’s law is found in all ages and never grows old. “Blessed be the God of truth.”

The main verse is 37: wine, the king, women and the children of men are wicked, and there is no truth in them. And men of understanding fell victim to it. Adam fell victim when it came to a woman, and so did David, Solomon and Ezekiel. God granted those men understanding, but wine and women make men of understanding to fall away.

sense.text: “Follow not thine own mind and thy strength, to walk in the ways of thy heart.” When you find yourself veering off into your sins, you start to follow your own mind, to do what you want to do, to walk in your own opinions, thoughts and emotions.

“And say not, Who shall controul me for my works?” Don’t say, who will tell me what to do, I’m not listening to any leaders, I’ll eat what I want, sleep with who I want, when I want. A brother walked in the other day and said he wasn’t coming back, it’s too hard, he’s tired. Tired after seven or eight years? There are men here who have been in this truth almost thirty years. Satan says to you, only you are tired, they don’t understand you, you’ve been alone eight or nine years with no woman and no warmth at home. I understand you. Come, let’s go out in the world where things are easier; you can have who you want, how many you want. America is going to be destroyed and we all die anyway, so go out with a bang. Take that purple off. They call you lazy and immature; I love you, no one loves you more than me. Look at her now: she can kill babies when she wants to; look what I gave her.

“For the Lord will surely revenge thy pride.” You are going to get it.

“Say not, I have sinned, and what harm hath happened unto me?” That is Satan in your head: you fornicated, you had two women last week, and you’re still here, your heart is still beating. That Bible is up to interpretation, they are a cult, I’m God, I’m talking to you now, you’re spiritual.

“For the Lord is longsuffering, he will in no wise let thee go.” You are not dead because God is patient with his chosen. He says, Satan, you can have him a little while, but I want him back. Some go out like the prodigal son and come back, but they don’t come back unscathed: they come back with child support, with a disease, from jail. And some God does not want back at all. You don’t want that.

“Concerning propitiation”: that is reconciliation, returning to God. “Be not without fear to add sin unto sin.” Don’t think that because you got away with it you can do it again and again. We play with sin the way a child keeps touching what his father told him to leave alone. After a while the Most High visits you: he lets Satan send his messengers, makes you see things, lets anger hop in you so you hit your wife or lose your job. Short-term decisions lead to long-term consequences, because you kept poking the bear.

“And say not, His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins.” That is Christianity: grace, grace, I’m delivered, I’m saved, I can do what I want. “For mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth upon sinners.” He is coming for you.

“Make no tarrying to turn to the Lord, and put not off from day to day.” If you fell away, return, and sooner rather than later. Some are sitting at home playing in their sin so they won’t come to the school, saying I’m spiritual by myself in front of my computer or the television. That is not biblical; that is Satan. You are watching the news, seeing what Trump is doing and the chariots they call drones mobilizing, all that has been taught these past years coming to pass, and you are still dragging your feet.

“For suddenly shall the wrath of the Lord come forth, and in thy security thou shalt be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.” Your security is your comfort and complacency. It will be too late.

“Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth.” It goes for the young woman too. Solomon wrote this, and he is being very sarcastic; our forefathers were sarcastic and God is sarcastic. Yeah, young man, have fun, YOLO: “walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes”, whatever you see and want, take it. “But know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.” You can do those things, but God will deal with you.

“Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh.” The sorrow is walking in the ways of your own heart and the sight of your own eyes, because that leads to destruction, damnation, consequences and repercussions.

“For childhood and youth are vanity.” You won’t stay young forever, and if you do something stupid enough in your youth, that youth goes fast. Youth means nothing in prison, nothing when your check is garnished and you walk out of court making ten dollars a week. A girl walking around fifteen or sixteen pregnant, her youth is over; and if she aborts it, the Most High will abort her.

precepts.why:
“Flee also youthful lusts.” Youthful lust is not only in young men. A grown man in his forties, fifties or sixties can still have that youthful lust in him, and young men have it as well. “But follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”

The point is to flee youthful lust. That is what Solomon spoke about in Ecclesiastes 11:9 and 10: young man, young woman, remove sorrow from your heart, because youthful lust leads to sorrow.

sense.text: “I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason of things.” Solomon had the same habit Adam had: he wanted to know more than he should have known. What they had on the table was not enough. “And to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness and madness”: Solomon wanted to explore wickedness, why man falls victim to it, what is so special about it. But to understand it, you must indulge in it to an extent.

“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands.” Not every woman, but the woman whose heart, her mind, is entrapment. Rappers, celebrities and rich men fall victim to these women who lie with them for the check, the fame and the security, who will dig the condom out of the garbage to get pregnant. “Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.”

“Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account.” The preacher is Solomon himself. He had a thousand women, seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he examined them one by one. “Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not”: he was looking for wisdom among his women and could not find it. “One man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.” The only wisdom he found among the thousand was himself; among all his women he found no wisdom, only evil.

So when they say a woman wrote the Song of Solomon, a black woman who said she was black, read Ecclesiastes. Solomon wrote the Song of Solomon. His wives were based on business relations: he took heathen daughters, from Pharaoh, from the Moabite king, the Edomite king, as gestures of alliance, as our kings did. And the wickedness that took him away came from his wives.

“Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright.” God made man to keep his laws and commandments. “But they have sought out many inventions.” Man says God doesn’t know what he’s doing, I know better: God made me a man, but I feel like a woman; I’m a woman, but I feel like a man; white man, come cut me open and give me a penis, cut the rod off and give me a vagina, because God doesn’t know what he’s talking about. That is the LGBTQ community: many inventions.

“Say not thou, It is through the Lord that I fell away.” Don’t say that because you messed up it is God’s fault, the truth’s fault: when I was in that Bible I had it easier, it was their interpretation that made me fall away, my testimony of being in that cult. We have heard this before from those who departed.

“For thou oughtest not to do the things that he hateth.” They leave out of here worse than they came in. If we are wicked and evil, why are you celebrating Halloween, Christmas and New Year again, why are the sisters back in pants and the brothers in dresses? You were good before you left; now you are bugged out, so the problem is not us. When you leave, the spirit you were in stays here. It is not a going-away prize. You leave, you stay gone, and you die gone.

“The Lord hateth all abomination; and they that fear God love it not.” Women in pants, men in dresses, homosexuality, incest, pedophilia, bestiality: we hate that, and we are not to ally ourselves with it.

“He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel.” He left Adam in the hand of his counsel: “If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.” To perform your faithfulness, you must keep the commandments. This proves faith comes with works. Faith is a performance, an action; your faith is proven by your actions, not your feelings.

“He hath set fire and water before thee: stretch forth thy hand unto whether thou wilt.” He set a decision before you: the fire, the death, or the water, the understanding. That is the free will of the Bible: do what I say or don’t, and I’ll bless you or I’ll kill you. “Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.”

But the decision you make, he knows already. It is predetermined, but it is not for you to know. God is the writer of the script and we are living it out; the prophets already saw the end and we are catching up to what they saw. You choose to be a nigga till you die, you are going to die. You choose that and then come back and the Lord receives you, or you stay righteous the whole time: we all reach the same destination, deliverance or death, fire or water.
“For the wisdom of the Lord is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholdeth all things.” He sees everything. “And his eyes are upon them that fear him, and he knoweth every work of man.”

“He hath commanded no man to do wickedly, neither hath he given any man licence to sin.” He gave no man or woman a commandment to do evil, and no permission to break his laws. Modern Christians say Christ died so we can do what we want, Christ kept all the commandments so we don’t have to. That is Christianity; it is not in the Bible.

“Say not thou, I will hide myself from the Lord.” Don’t say you will do things in secret and it won’t be exposed. Over time, when it is evil enough and the Most High wants it known, it will be made known.

“Shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembered among so many people.” You think that because millions out there sin and do worse, God will exempt you: I’m just battling porn, people out here murder, steal, lie and sell drugs. God says don’t think like that, because I expect more from you than from them. I hold you to a higher standard. I can call them out of that, but I already called you: you are already on the payroll, and you are being insubordinate. “For what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?” Who am I, we all sin, why are my sins so important? That is the evil thought.

“Behold, the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, the deep, and the earth, and all that therein is, shall be moved when he shall visit.” When he shows up, everybody will know he is here, and no matter where you hide, he will find you.

“But they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way.” The wine and strong drink here are not literally liquor; they are sin. The Lord through the prophets uses wine for sin because it is an influence: driving drunk is driving under the influence. Sin is very influential in every facet, through music, TV, media, billboards, food and porn. Your eyes, ears and mind are easily influenced, and sin puts spirits on you, or puts you in a certain spirit. So God compares sin to wine and strong drink.

“The priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine”: consumed in their sin, under the influence. “They err in vision”: they lie, they sin in their own thoughts. “They stumble in judgment”: they don’t judge righteously but after their own hearts, because they are consumed in their strong drink and their falsehoods. This is the wine of wine and women that make men of understanding fall away.

precepts.why:
This is the precept of what wine is, so no one says it is just an interpretation. “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink”. A man walks in the spirit of falsehood and lies, and prophesies wine and strong drink: so wine and strong drink are falsehood and lies.

Christianity, Buddhism, Islam and politics are falsehood and lies. There are people we love within those ideologies, but the ideologies are falsehood, and they have a major influence on the world. Music today and politics today fall into the category of wine and strong drink.

“Stay yourselves, and wonder; cry ye out, and cry.” Stay yourselves means study and remain steadfast; cry out means go out and teach. “They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.” Our people are drunken, but not with wine. How do we stumble and stagger? Under the influence of sin. That is how we are drunken.

sense.text: “Thy sons have fainted”: unconscious, asleep. “They lie at the head of all the streets”: the hoods, the corners, the ghettos and the slums. “As a wild bull in a net”: violent and fierce, and oppressed. “They are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God”: angry and violent, under the cursing of our God.

“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” We are the afflicted and we are the drunken, but not with wine: our people on the corners of the streets are drunken, but it is with sin.

precepts.why:
This shows what happens to the young men who faint at the head of the streets. Of the three men before the king, the first “had spoken of the strength of wine”, and here it is speaking of actual liquor: “how exceeding strong is wine! it causeth all men to err that drink it.” It causes all men to sin that drink it to excess.

“It maketh the mind of the king and of the fatherless child to be all one; of the bondman and of the freeman, of the poor man and of the rich.” The influence of liquor puts a king in the same mindset as a fatherless child; whatever their status, drunk to excess, all men behave alike. “It turneth also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembereth neither sorrow nor debt”: when black folks can’t pay the bills, they buy beer or liquor and drink their worries away. “So that a man remembereth neither king nor governor”: you forget the authority, the police, all the authorities of the world. “And it maketh to speak all things by talents”: it is a truth serum; you say things you would never say sober. Careless, carefree, open and honest.

“And when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and brethren, and a little after draw out swords”: no loyalty to friends or family, and then violent. “But when they are from the wine, they remember not what they have done.” Like the fifteen-year-old who killed another boy and cried when the judge denied his parole: there was no thought of consequence beforehand, because the fatherless child is carefree, with no care for authority, open and honest enough to rap about what he did. Then he wants his lawyer.

“Is not wine the strongest, that enforceth to do thus?” That goes back to Isaiah, the sons lying in the streets as a wild bull in a net. The child who walks around with no father at home has the same attributes: no care for authority, happy, jolly, carefree, open, honest, forgetting what he did, crying in the end, not loyal to friends or family, killing his brother, going against his parents. Fatherless children are like drunkards.

sense.text: We are still in wine and women, the temptations and the influence of sin. “Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes? They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.” Drink enough wine and the whites of your eyes turn red.
“Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup.” Don’t be enamored with how beautiful the bottle is and how dark red the wine looks. Don’t fall for that.

“At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.” In the end it bites you. You keep drinking something that seems light, this ain’t nothing, and it gets you. It is the same with sin: you play with it and it starts off light, I watch porn once in a while, then once a week, twice, every day, every hour. It evolves like liquor. You keep sipping the strong drink, the sin, until you are under the influence and lost in it, in front of the computer going from one video to the next, look up at five and it is ten.

“Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.” Under the influence your eyes behold strange women: wine and women again, as in Hosea 4 and Sirach 19, always used together, because wine and sin go hand in hand. In this context the strange women are your porn, or women of other nations, or back-door marriages.

“Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.” A mast is the tall upright post on a ship, the lookout high up on the boat. Under the influence of sin or liquor you are like a person floating in the middle of the sea, in dangerous waters, or one lying at the top of the mast who could fall out and die. You are in a dangerous position.

“They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not.” You were drunk and acting crazy, got punched in the face, and felt nothing; you wake up missing a tooth with your eye black. It is the same with sin: so lost in it you forget what you did, and you wake up with your hand in your pants and the TV playing.

“When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.” You wake up beaten and stricken, and you go right back to it tomorrow. It is the same behavior as the fatherless child.

precepts.why:
The serpent’s bite of the wine is sin. “My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins.” Maybe you sinned today or yesterday: stop, and ask the Lord to forgive you. “Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” It will rip you apart if you give in.

We all have our battles and our inner demons, and the Lord sees when you are fighting to fend it off. Often we fall when we are alone, and Satan comes knocking around three or four in the morning, when the mind is more open and the imagination runs wild. The Lord sees that you are trying, but that is not an excuse; at some point you have to stop it. Like a drug, you wean yourself over time. Find something else to do with your time: watch a class, go on Clubhouse, listen to audio, read your four chapters, go over your notes and add them to your Bible. When your hands are idle they do what they shouldn’t.

“All iniquity is as a twoedged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.” It cuts both ways: you hurt yourself, and if you get so lost in your sin that you give up the fight, you hurt those around you who love you and tried to help you.

sense.text: “It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink.” Some scholars say Lemuel is another name for Solomon, and his mother is teaching him. Kings and princes are set up to judge matters and govern the people, and you cannot be in your right mind under strong drink. It is not good to drink when it is time to judge or teach your people. There are Israelites on video sitting with scotch and bourbon in a glass, sunglasses indoors, teaching the Bible.

“Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.” They forget the law, forget how to teach the Bible properly, which they do, and pervert the judgment of our people. They pervert the Bible itself.

“For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways.” In this truth you have to learn to wean yourself off. When you first came through the doors you were still battling what you were battling, and wisdom walked with you in your crooked ways. As you learn, study and apply, you begin to change: “and bring fear and dread upon him.” Fear and dread enter you: I can’t do that anymore. You change your friends, how you dress, how you behave, how you speak.

“And torment him with her discipline.” What you got away with in the world you can’t do anymore, because now the Most High is holding you accountable. Discipline is torment: it is structure and order, pressure applied to the flesh. In the world you did what the flesh wanted; with God’s laws it is a battle: I can’t watch that, I can’t see her anymore, I can’t be around them. The Bishop has said, I’m not always motivated, but I always stay disciplined. Discipline is not fun and not easy. “Until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws”: until she can trust you to do right by her and teach her to the rest of the people, and she puts you through a trial.

“Then will she return the straight way unto him.” Before you walked in crooked ways; now you walk the straight path. Crooked is easy, straight is harder, but better, because it leads to life. “And comfort him, and shew him her secrets”: the deep, dark sayings. Adam and Eve, America in the Bible, nuclear wars, Trump’s policies, the slave ship, America’s destruction and World War III in the Bible; understanding of Genesis, of Revelation, of the law. In the midst of the torment of discipline you are comforted by learning and applying new things, growing and evolving.

“But if he go wrong, she will forsake him.” Here is the stipulation: if you turn your back on it and give up the fight, she forsakes you. You leave, but the spirit stays here. If you came in as Tyrone and became Azariah and decide to leave, you leave as Tyrone again; Azariah stays here. “And give him over to his own ruin”: your own ruin, not ours. As they said at an old job, we don’t fire you, you fire you.

“Observe the opportunity, and beware of evil.” Observe the opportunity you have here while you still have it. “And be not ashamed when it concerneth thy soul.” When it comes to what you are battling, make yourself open to communicate. Speak to someone, a counsel, about it. Don’t hold it inside, or wisdom will leave you and it will take hold of you and you will be gone.

“My son, if thou wilt, thou shalt be taught.” Our people must learn how to learn, how to be taught. That is one of the main things in this truth: you must want to be taught. Come in here a know-it-all, a smart ass, and you won’t last long; if you know everything, why are you here? “And if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be prudent”: prudent, and not impudent.

“If thou love to hear, thou shalt receive understanding.” Because of their sins and lust, some begin to hate to hear; they lose the desire of loving to hear. “And if thou bow thine ear, thou shalt be wise.”

“Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise.” Put yourself around the seniors: the officers, the soldiers, the captains, the deacons, the Bishops. Be in the company of those men if you can, and sisters, be around the aged women, if you are given the opportunity.

“Be willing to hear every godly discourse.” Hear every godly conversation, so you push out the porn and scrape it out. You may not get all of it out, but try. “And let not the parables of understanding escape thee”: don’t remove yourself from the parables spoken by the leadership.

“But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.” Make it your job to be an example, and not to offend the little ones and cause them to go astray.
“Woe unto the world because of offences!” Because of sin. “For it must needs be that offences come”: it is not a matter of if, but when. “But woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!”

“Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee.” Whatever is close to you that keeps you from applying God’s laws and commandments, a relative, a brother or sister, a father or mother, porn, drugs, alcohol, food: cut it off. Your hand and your foot are what you desire most and what is important to you, and if they cause you to offend, cut them off. “It is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed”, with those things cut off, “rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire”, keeping the sins and giving into them.

“And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee.” You want your eye; it is close to you and you need it. But if it causes you to offend, the liquor, the food, the porn, the prostitutes, the OnlyFans, cut it out. Christ is saying stop doing it. “It is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire”: the second death, to die and then die again.

Right now we are under grace; we have mercy by the blood of the lamb. But don’t use that as an excuse. God gave no man licence to sin, so at some point you have to learn to quench those things and mortify them.

“A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house.” He doesn’t keep his promises and his vows. “If he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he maketh a double offence.” When you don’t acknowledge your problem, you make it worse. When you pretend you have it all together and you don’t, you add a double offence. That is why we read, be not ashamed when it concerneth thy soul. Any brother who says he didn’t go through anything in here, online or offline, is a liar: a double offence.

“And if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.” Make false promises and false vows you don’t keep, and you will find yourself in trouble.

“For there is a shame that bringeth sin.” That is your secret sins: your porn, the evil you are involved in, your lust, whatever it is. You know what it is, and you are ashamed of it.

“And there is a shame which is glory and grace.” That is the shame of confessing it. When you acknowledge it, speak on it, see it as a problem, get counsel for it and fight it, whether homosexuality, violence or drug abuse, it brings shame and you are embarrassed. But because you acknowledged it and spoke to your counselor, it brings forth glory, the kingdom, and grace, mercy, as opposed to the double offence.
“Whoso feareth the Lord will receive his discipline; and they that seek him early shall find favour.” Seek him early: make no tarrying, seek him fast, and you will find favour.
“He that seeketh the law shall be filled therewith: but the hypocrite will be offended thereat.” The hypocrite is angry and offended when he is corrected, even at this class.
“They that fear the Lord shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.” They will be able to judge matters.
“A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will.” The sinful man or woman will not be corrected, but finds an excuse according to what they want to do.
“He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” Trust in God and you will fare never the worse; you will do a lot better.

“To terrify and do wrong will waste riches: thus the house of proud men shall be made desolate.” A lot of brothers out there who are well off, and these celebrities, waste their riches, their blessings, because they are all in sin.

“A prayer out of a poor man’s mouth reacheth to the ears of God, and his judgment cometh speedily.” A poor man’s mouth is a poor spirit, a contrite and humble heart: Lord, I’m battling, have mercy upon me, help me battle this. God sees that you are sincere.

“He that hateth to be reproved is in the way of sinners.” When you hate correction and find an excuse, you are in the way of sinners. “But he that feareth the Lord will repent from his heart”: sincerely, not out of a grudge or anger or because someone said so, but because you know so and you acknowledge it.

“An eloquent man is known far and near”: by how he carries himself, how he speaks, how he teaches and how he judges a matter. “But a man of understanding knoweth when he slippeth.” Whether you are messing up, when you are going through things, only you know.
